stem: Microscopy later shows that an arthropod recorded as a probable spider mite was actually a different mite. What should happen to the earlier record?
choices: Overwrite the original observation so no incorrect hypothesis remains.
Preserve the original observation and confidence state, append the corrected identification and supporting evidence, and document how the workup changed.
Delete all earlier scouting because the diagnosis changed.
Keep both identities listed as confirmed.
rationale: Data-integrity practice preserves the original record and subsequent correction so the diagnostic history remains reconstructable rather than rewritten after new evidence arrives.
